intent: The icon-only button that toggles the nearest SidebarProvider's sidebar.
typical_uses: The toggle at the start of the main area's header

dont_use_when.situation: A toggle that should read as the panel's edge rather than a button

invariants.text: SidebarTrigger is the kit's Button with a fixed panel icon; a `variant` or `size` passed to it replaces the defaults.
`label` becomes the button's `aria-label`; an explicit `aria-label` passed alongside it wins.
A consumer `onClick` runs first and the sidebar toggles after it on every click; the handler cannot prevent the toggle.
The trigger reads the provider through useSidebar, so it works at any depth inside SidebarProvider and throws outside one.

anti_patterns.dont: Restyle SidebarTrigger into a different control
anti_patterns.do_instead: Build a Button whose onClick calls `toggleSidebar` from useSidebar

a11y.by: sidebar.test.tsx finds the trigger by role button with the name "Toggle Sidebar" (its default `label`) and asserts a click collapses the sidebar

rtl.by: sidebar.tsx renders a fixed PanelLeftIcon with no direction handling, and sidebar.md records that it is not mirrored under a right-to-left direction

render.states: render replaces the rendered element with one the caller supplies
render.because: Base UI's render prop takes an element or a function of the button's own state, so its type is a union of a React element and a callback - the compiler emits one JSON type per property.

style.states: style accepts a function of the button's state as well as a plain style object
style.because: Base UI widens React's `CSSProperties` to `CSSProperties | ((state) => CSSProperties)` so a caller can style off the primitive's own state (disabled). The compiler emits one JSON type per property, so nothing is asserted; the kit's own styling goes through button.module.css and sidebar.module.css, not through this.

good.title: The default trigger in the main area
An accessible name of its own

bad.title: A caption passed as children
bad.why: SidebarTrigger omits `children` from its props and renders a fixed icon; the caption is a type error, and the accessible name comes from `label`.

The compiler emits one JSON type per property; this type is left to tsc. render replaces the rendered element with one the caller supplies.
